_provenance.notes: The Southeast Alaska (SEAK) troll fishery targets Chinook and coho salmon using hook-and-line gear (trolling). SEAK troll Chinook are caught during a winter troll season (October-April) and a summer season (July-September). The Pacific Salmon Treaty (US-Canada) allocates Chinook harvest between SEAK troll and Canadian fisheries. SEAK troll Chinook is the highest-value-per-fish commercial salmon fishery in Alaska — a troll-caught Chinook can be delivered fresh/iced to premium markets for $8-12/lb ex-vessel vs $3-5/lb for net-caught.

pst_allocation_context.description: Pacific Salmon Treaty Chinook allocation — SEAK troll annual limits
pst_allocation_context.notes: SEAK troll Chinook is governed by the Pacific Salmon Treaty (1985, renegotiated 1999, 2009, 2019). Annual catch ceilings for SEAK are set in the treaty annex, based on aggregate abundance indices. When abundance is low, SEAK trollers take cuts first.
